title: Network Policies

header.html: Kubernetes v1.37.0 with kindnet, which enforces NetworkPolicy (tested: traffic was blocked after a deny policy)

toc.title: The AND versus OR trap (most tested detail)

html:
1The model in six sentences

  1. By default all Pods accept all traffic (and send all traffic).
  2. A NetworkPolicy selects Pods with podSelector and says which directions it governs in policyTypes (Ingress, Egress, or both).
  3. Once any policy selects a Pod for a direction, that direction is default deny for the Pod, and only what the policies allow gets through.
  4. Policies are additive: the allowed traffic is the union of all policies that select the Pod. There are no deny rules.
  5. Policies are namespaced: a policy protects Pods in its own namespace only.
  6. Allowed traffic is described by peers (from for ingress, to for egress) and ports.

2Anatomy

apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: {name: db-allow-backend, namespace: shop}
spec:
  podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: db}}      # WHO is protected (empty {} = every Pod in the namespace)
  policyTypes: [Ingress]                     # which directions this policy governs
  ingress:
  - from:                                    # WHO may connect
    - podSelector: {matchLabels: {role: backend}}
    ports:                                   # to WHICH ports
    - {protocol: TCP, port: 80}
Peer type Selects
podSelector Pods with these labels in the policy's own namespace
namespaceSelector all Pods in namespaces with these labels
namespaceSelector + podSelector in the same item Pods with these labels in namespaces with these labels (AND)
ipBlock an IP range (cidr, optional except); use for traffic outside the cluster

3The AND versus OR trap (most tested detail)

ingress:
- from:
  - namespaceSelector: {matchLabels: {zone: trusted}}   # item 1 ... 
    podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: client}}           # ... same item: AND

ingress:
- from:
  - namespaceSelector: {matchLabels: {zone: trusted}}   # item 1: any Pod in trusted namespaces
  - podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: client}}           # item 2: OR app=client Pods in THIS namespace

A dash (-) starts a new peer. Two selectors under one dash = AND; two dashes = OR. Lab 9.5 tests both forms.

4Common recipes

Deny all ingress to every Pod in a namespace:

spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: [Ingress]

(no ingress: rules at all). Same with Egress to deny all outgoing traffic.

Allow all ingress: ingress: [{}] (one empty rule) with policyTypes: [Ingress].

Allow from a namespace: namespaceSelector: {matchLabels: {team: frontend}}. Label the namespace if needed: k label ns fe team=frontend. Every namespace also has the automatic label kubernetes.io/metadata.name=<name>, handy when you have no label to use.

Restrict egress but keep DNS working. Once egress is restricted, Pods can no longer ask CoreDNS, so name lookups fail. Always allow port 53 in both protocols:

egress:
- to:
  - podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: db}}
  ports: [{protocol: TCP, port: 80}]
- ports:
  - {protocol: UDP, port: 53}
  - {protocol: TCP, port: 53}

5Reading and debugging

k -n np4 get netpol
k -n np4 describe netpol backend-in        # shows selected Pods and rules in words
k -n np4 get pods --show-labels            # labels are the usual bug
k -n np4 exec frontend -- wget -qO- -T3 http://backend    # timeout = blocked

A blocked connection times out (no "connection refused"). Typical bugs: label typos (role: front versus role: frontend; Lab 9.4), a selector in the wrong namespace, a missing ports entry, forgetting DNS in an egress policy, or the policy's podSelector not matching the target Pods.

The exam tasks focus on Pod-to-Pod rules; read the task for the namespace and the labels of both sides.

6Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m09 -->

Lab 9.1: default deny

Domain: Networking | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m09-01-default-deny)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace np1, the Pod web (nginx) and the Pod client (busybox) can talk to each other. Create a NetworkPolicy named default-deny-ingress that blocks all incoming traffic to every Pod in the namespace and allows nothing. Outgoing traffic is not restricted.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n np1 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: {name: default-deny-ingress}
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
Y
sleep 5

Lab 9.2: allow from namespace

Domain: Networking | Points: 7 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m09-02-allow-from-namespace)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace np2, the Pod api (nginx, port 80) must accept TCP traffic on port 80 only from Pods in namespaces that carry the label team=frontend. Everything else must be denied. The namespace fe has the label team=frontend and the namespace other does not. Create one NetworkPolicy named api-from-frontend in np2.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n np2 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: {name: api-from-frontend}
spec:
  podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: api}}
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector: {matchLabels: {team: frontend}}
    ports:
    - {protocol: TCP, port: 80}
Y
sleep 5

Lab 9.3: egress policy

Domain: Networking | Points: 8 | Time: about 9 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m09-03-egress-policy)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace np3, the Pod app (busybox) must only be allowed to send traffic to (a) Pods labelled app=db on TCP port 80 and (b) the cluster DNS on port 53 (UDP and TCP). All other outgoing traffic from app must be blocked. Create one NetworkPolicy named app-egress for the Pod app.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n np3 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: {name: app-egress}
spec:
  podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: app}}
  policyTypes: [Egress]
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: db}}
    ports:
    - {protocol: TCP, port: 80}
  - ports:
    - {protocol: UDP, port: 53}
    - {protocol: TCP, port: 53}
Y
sleep 5

Lab 9.4: fix policy labels

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 7 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m09-04-fix-policy-labels)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace np4, the Pod backend should be reachable on port 80 from the Pod frontend (label role=frontend), but requests fail since a NetworkPolicy was added. Fix the NetworkPolicy backend-in (keep its name; do not delete or relabel the Pods) so that frontend can reach backend while the Pod intruder (label role=intruder) still cannot.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n np4 get netpol backend-in -o yaml | grep -A3 "from:"
kubectl -n np4 get pods --show-labels
kubectl -n np4 patch netpol backend-in --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/ingress/0/from/0/podSelector/matchLabels","value":{"role":"frontend"}}]'
sleep 5

Lab 9.5: and vs or selectors

Domain: Networking | Points: 8 | Time: about 9 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m09-05-and-vs-or-selectors)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace np5, the Pod vault (nginx, port 80) must accept traffic only from Pods labelled app=client that run in a namespace labelled zone=trusted (both conditions must be true for the same Pod). Pods labelled app=client in other namespaces, and other Pods in the trusted namespace, must be denied. Create one NetworkPolicy named vault-in.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n np5 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: {name: vault-in}
spec:
  podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: vault}}
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector: {matchLabels: {zone: trusted}}
      podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: client}}
Y
sleep 5

Lab 9.6: deny all allow dns

Domain: Networking | Points: 8 | Time: about 9 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m09-06-deny-all-allow-dns)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace np6, the Pod client (busybox) must be locked down completely except for name resolution: block all ingress and all egress for every Pod in the namespace, then allow egress on port 53 (UDP and TCP) so that DNS still works. Use NetworkPolicies (one named deny-all, one named allow-dns). Afterwards the client must still resolve web.np6.svc.cluster.local but must not be able to fetch the page from web.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n np6 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: {name: deny-all}
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: [Ingress, Egress]
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: {name: allow-dns}
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: [Egress]
  egress:
  - ports:
    - {protocol: UDP, port: 53}
    - {protocol: TCP, port: 53}
Y
sleep 5

<!-- /LABS -->

7Recall questions

R1What is the default network behavior without any policy?

Show the answer

All traffic between Pods is allowed.

R2What happens to ingress for a Pod once a policy with policyTypes: [Ingress] selects it?

Show the answer

Ingress becomes default deny except what the policies allow.

R3What does an empty podSelector: {} in spec select?

Show the answer

Every Pod in the policy's namespace.

R4Two selectors in the same from item, versus two items: what is the difference?

Show the answer

Same item is AND; separate items are OR.

R5How do you allow traffic from another namespace?

Show the answer

With a namespaceSelector on that namespace's labels (label the namespace if needed).

R6Why does an egress policy often break name resolution, and how do you fix it?

Show the answer

It blocks traffic to CoreDNS; allow UDP and TCP port 53 in an egress rule.

R7How does a blocked connection look to the client?

Show the answer

It times out.

R8Can a NetworkPolicy protect Pods in a different namespace than its own?

Show the answer

No; it governs only Pods in its own namespace.

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
Default allow all; first policy makes the selected direction deny-by-default
Spec podSelector, policyTypes, ingress.from, egress.to, ports
Peers podSelector, namespaceSelector, ipBlock
AND / OR one dash = AND, separate dashes = OR
Deny all podSelector: {} plus policyTypes and no rules
Egress always allow DNS 53 (UDP and TCP)
Debug describe netpol, get pods --show-labels, wget -T3 from a client
